headline: OpenAI's GPT models launching on Google Cloud and Antigravity
summary: OpenAI's latest GPT 6 and 6.1 models (Astra, Sol, Luna) will soon be available on Google Cloud, expanding enterprise options beyond Gemini and Claude.
details: Google Cloud is set to integrate OpenAI's cutting-edge GPT 6 and 6.1 models, including Astra, Sol, and Luna, in the coming weeks. This move significantly broadens the AI model offerings within Google's "Model Garden," which already hosts Gemini, Mistral, Llama, Gemma, and Anthropic's Claude.

This partnership makes Google Cloud the sole provider offering access to all three leading closed large language models. While Microsoft remains OpenAI's primary cloud partner, this deal allows businesses to run OpenAI models entirely on Google's infrastructure, with transactions managed through the Google Cloud Marketplace.

The integration aims to provide enterprise customers with more flexibility, allowing dynamic workload movement between different LLMs based on performance, latency, and efficiency needs. Astra, being the most advanced, is expected to have the highest running costs.

OpenAI models are rolling out now in a private preview for select enterprise clients, accessible via API. This includes users of Codex CLI and Codex Desktop, with inference handled by Google's systems.

Beyond enterprise solutions, the OpenAI models are also slated for integration into Google's agent-powered coding tool, Antigravity. Previously, Antigravity supported Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude, and the addition of OpenAI models will further enhance its capabilities.
